facts.statement: Dilophosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically from the Sinemurian to Toarcian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic (Sinemurian–Toarcian),

facts.statement: Three Dilophosaurus skeletons were discovered in northern Arizona in 1940, with the two best-preserved specimens collected in 1942.
facts.quote: Three skeletons were discovered in northern Arizona in 1940, and the two best preserved were collected in 1942.

facts.statement: Samuel P. Welles named the most complete specimen *Megalosaurus wetherilli* in 1954.
facts.quote: The most complete specimen became the holotype of a new species in the genus Megalosaurus, named M. wetherilli by Samuel P. Welles in 1954.

facts.statement: Samuel P. Welles discovered a larger skeleton of the same species in 1964.
facts.quote: Welles found a larger skeleton in the same region belonging to the same species in 1964.

facts.statement: In 1970, Samuel P. Welles reclassified the species into the new genus *Dilophosaurus* due to the presence of skull crests.
facts.quote: Realizing it bore crests on its skull, he assigned the species to the new genus Dilophosaurus in 1970, as Dilophosaurus wetherilli.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was approximately 7 meters long and weighed about 400 kilograms.
facts.quote: At about 7 m in length, with a weight of about 400 kg, Dilophosaurus was one of the earliest large predatory dinosaurs

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had a slender, lightly built body and a proportionally large skull.
facts.quote: It was slender and lightly built, and the skull was proportionally large.

facts.statement: The teeth of Dilophosaurus were long, curved, thin, and compressed sideways.
facts.quote: The teeth were long, curved, thin, and compressed sideways.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was likely an active, bipedal predator that may have hunted large animals, as well as smaller animals and fish.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus would have been active and bipedal, and may have hunted large animals; it could also have fed on smaller animals and fish.

facts.statement: The function of Dilophosaurus crests is unknown, but they were likely used for visual displays like species recognition or sexual selection rather than combat.
facts.quote: The function of the crests is unknown; they were too weak for battle, but may have been used in visual display, such as species recognition and sexual selection.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus may have grown rapidly, gaining 30 to 35 kilograms per year in its early life.
facts.quote: It may have grown rapidly, attaining a growth rate of 30 to 35 kg per year early in life.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Charles L. Camp led a UCMP expedition to Navajo County, Arizona, in the summer of 1942.
facts.quote: In the summer of 1942, the paleontologist Charles L. Camp led a field party from the University of California Museum of Paleontology (UCMP) in search of fossil vertebrates in Navajo County in northern Arizona.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Kayenta Formation, located about 20 miles north of Cameron near Tuba City.
facts.quote: The area was part of the Kayenta Formation, about 20 mi north of Cameron near Tuba City in the Navajo Indian Reservation.

facts.statement: Three skeletons were found arranged in a triangle measuring about 30 feet on one side.
facts.quote: Three dinosaur skeletons were found in purplish shale, arranged in a triangle, about 30 ft long at one side.

facts.statement: Specimen UCMP 37302 was designated the holotype and UCMP 37303 the paratype.
facts.quote: The nearly complete specimen (catalogued as UCMP 37302) was made the holotype of the species, and the second specimen (UCMP 37303) was made the paratype.

facts.statement: Welles initially placed the species in *Megalosaurus* because of similar limb proportions to *M. bucklandii* and a lack of perceived differences.
facts.quote: Welles placed the new species in Megalosaurus due to the similar limb proportions of it and M. bucklandii, and because he did not find great differences between them.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus is considered a member of the family Dilophosauridae, though this classification is debated by some researchers.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus has been considered a member of the family Dilophosauridae along with Dracovenator, a group placed between the Coelophysidae and later theropods, but some researchers have not found support for this grouping.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus lived in North America during the Early Jurassic, approximately 186 million years ago.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus ( ) is a genus of theropod dinosaurs that lived in what is now North America during the Early Jurassic, about 186 million years ago.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was designated the state dinosaur of Connecticut based on fossil tracks found there.
facts.quote: It was designated as the state dinosaur of Connecticut based on tracks found there.

facts.statement: The genus name Dilophosaurus was coined in 1970 by Welles, derived from Greek words meaning "two-crested lizard".
facts.quote: In 1970, Welles coined the new genus name Dilophosaurus, from the Greek words di (δι) meaning "two", lophos (λόφος) meaning "crest", and sauros (σαυρος) meaning "lizard": "two-crested lizard".

facts.statement: In 2020, Marsh and Rowe comprehensively redescribed Dilophosaurus, including the previously undescribed specimen UCMP 77270 from 1964.
facts.quote: In 2020, the paleontologists Adam D. Marsh and Timothy B. Rowe comprehensively redescribed Dilophosaurus based on the by then known specimens, including specimen UCMP 77270 which had remained undescribed since 1964.

facts.statement: In 1993, paleontologist Shaojin Hu named the Chinese skeleton D. sinensis as a new species of Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: The paleontologist Shaojin Hu named it as a new species of Dilophosaurus in 1993, D. sinensis (from Greek Sinai, referring to China).

facts.statement: Marsh and Rowe concluded in 2020 that all known Dilophosaurus specimens belong to a single taxon, with differences attributed to maturity and preservation.
facts.quote: Marsh and Rowe concluded in 2020 that there was only one taxon among known Dilophosaurus specimens, and that differences between them were due to their different degree of maturity and preservation.

facts.statement: In 1998, Lamanna and colleagues determined that D. sinensis is identical to Sinosaurus triassicus, leading to its reclassification.
facts.quote: In 1998, the paleontologist Matthew C. Lamanna and colleagues found D. sinensis to be identical to Sinosaurus triassicus, a theropod from the same formation, named in 1940.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was the largest-known land animal in North America during the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: It was also the largest-known land animal of North America during the Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was slender and lightly built, with a size comparable to a brown bear.
facts.quote: Slender and lightly built, its size was comparable to that of a brown bear.

facts.statement: Other researchers interpret the same impressions as sedimentological artifacts, though this view does not exclude the possibility that the animal had feathers.
facts.quote: Other researchers instead interpret these impressions as sedimentological artifacts created as the dinosaur moved, though this interpretation does not rule out that the track-maker could have borne feathers.

facts.statement: In 2017, Wang and colleagues suggested that the species formerly known as D. sinensis might be a separate species, S. sinensis, despite agreeing it belongs in the genus Sinosaurus.
facts.quote: Guo-Fu Wang and colleagues agreed the species belonged in Sinosaurus in 2017, they suggested it may be a separate species, S. sinensis.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus possessed a pair of high, thin, arched crests running along the top of its skull.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus bore a pair of high, thin, and arched (or plate-shaped) crests longitudinally on the skull roof.

facts.statement: The crests were formed primarily by expanded nasal and lacrimal bones originating as ridges on the premaxillae.
facts.quote: The crests (termed the nasolacrimal crests) began as low ridges on the premaxillae and were mainly formed by the upwards expanded nasal and lacrimal bones.

facts.statement: Researchers estimate the crests may have extended up to approximately 12 mm above the skull based on preserved bone fragments.
facts.quote: Since only a short part of the upper surface of this process is unbroken, the rest of the crest may have risen above the skull over a distance of ~12 mm.

facts.statement: Scientists have debated whether the crests were bare bone or covered in keratin, with some comparing them to a double-crested cassowary.
facts.quote: Welles found the crests reminiscent of a double-crested cassowary, while Marsh and Rowe stated they were probably covered in keratin or keratinized skin.

facts.statement: CT scans revealed that air sacs were present in the bones surrounding the brain and connected to frontal sinus cavities.
facts.quote: CT scans show that air sacs (pockets of air that provide strength for and lighten bones) were present in the bones that surrounded the brain, and were continuous with the sinus cavities in the front of the skull.

facts.statement: The lower jaw was slender at the front but became massive at the skull connection and deep near the side opening.
facts.quote: The mandible was slender at the front, but the articular region (where it connected with the skull) was massive, and the mandible was deep around the mandibular fenestra (an opening on its side).

facts.statement: The front part of the lower jaw featured an up-curved chin rather than a pointed one.
facts.quote: The dentary bone (the front part of the mandible where most of the teeth there were attached) had an up-curved rather than pointed chin.

facts.statement: The skull contained four teeth in the premaxilla, twelve in the maxilla, and seventeen in the dentary.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus had four teeth in each premaxilla, 12 in each maxilla, and 17 in each dentary.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus teeth were generally long, thin, and curved backward with small bases.
facts.quote: The teeth were generally long, thin, and recurved, with relatively small bases.

facts.statement: The teeth were covered in a thin enamel layer ranging from 0.1 to 0.15 mm in thickness.
facts.quote: The teeth were covered in a thin layer of enamel, 0.1 to 0.15 mm thick, which extended far towards their bases.

facts.statement: The teeth had between 31 and 41 serrations on the front edges and 29 to 33 on the back edges.
facts.quote: About 31 to 41 serrations were on the front edges, and 29 to 33 were on the back.

facts.statement: The jaws held replacement teeth at various stages of eruption alongside functional teeth.
facts.quote: The jaws contained replacement teeth at various stages of eruption.

facts.statement: The plates separating the teeth between the jaws were very low.
facts.quote: The interdental plates between the teeth were very low.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus possessed 10 neck vertebrae, 14 back vertebrae, and 45 tail vertebrae, with air sacs extending into the bones.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus had 10 cervical (neck), 14 dorsal (back), and 45 caudal (tail) vertebrae, and air sacs grew into the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Dilophosaurus had a long neck flexed nearly 90 degrees to hold its skull in a horizontal position.
facts.quote: It had a long neck, which was probably flexed nearly 90° by the skull and by the shoulder, holding the skull in a horizontal posture.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Dilophosaurus had low spines that formed a distinctive Maltese cross shape when viewed from above.
facts.quote: The centra and neural spines of the cervical vertebrae were long and low, and the spines were stepped in side view, forming "shoulders" at the front and back, as well as taller, central "caps" that gave the appearance of a Maltese cross (cruciform) when seen from above, distinctive features of this dinosaur.

facts.statement: The shoulder blades of Dilophosaurus were uniquely wide and rectangular at the upper part.
facts.quote: The scapulae were wide, particularly the upper part, which was rectangular (or squared off), a unique feature.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had four fingers on its hands, with the first being short and strong with a large claw, while the other two were longer and slender with smaller claws.
facts.quote: The hands had four fingers: the first was shorter but stronger than the following two fingers, with a large claw, and the two following fingers were longer and slenderer, with smaller claws.

facts.statement: The third finger of Dilophosaurus was reduced, and the fourth finger was vestigial and non-functional.
facts.quote: The third finger was reduced, and the fourth was vestigial (retained, but without function).

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had large hind legs where the thigh bone was slightly longer than the lower leg bone, unlike Coelophysis.
facts.quote: The hind legs were large, with a slighter longer femur (thigh bone) than tibia (lower leg bone), the opposite of, for example, Coelophysis.

facts.statement: The massive thigh bone of Dilophosaurus had an S-shaped shaft with a greater trochanter centered on it.
facts.quote: The femur was massive; its shaft was sigmoid-shaped (curved like an 'S'), and its greater trochanter was centered on the shaft.

facts.statement: In Dilophosaurus, the lower end of the ischium was much more expanded than the foot of the pubic bone, and the ischium had a very thin shaft.
facts.quote: The foot of the pubic bone was only slightly expanded, whereas the lower end was much more expanded on the ischium, which also had a very thin shaft.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had large hind legs with a femur that was slightly longer than the tibia, contrasting with the proportions seen in Coelophysis.
facts.quote: The hind legs were large, with a slighter longer femur (thigh bone) than tibia (lower leg bone), the opposite of, for example, Coelophysis.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus belongs to the superfamily Coelophysoidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Coelophysoidea

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus is classified within the family Dilophosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dilophosauridae

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus fossils date back to the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Inferior

facts.statement: Megalosaurus wetherilli Welles, 1954 and Dilophosaurus breedorum are listed as synonyms for Dilophosaurus wetherilli.
facts.quote: synonyms: Megalosaurus wetherilli Welles, 1954 Dilophosaurus breedorum

facts.statement: The first specimens were described in 1954, but the genus received its current name a decade later.
facts.quote: Los primeros especímenes fueron descritos en 1954, pero no fue hasta una década más tarde que el género recibió su nombre actual.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus is now considered a member of the family Dilophosauridae, a group located between coelophysids and later theropods.
facts.quote: Hoy es considerado un miembro de la familia Dilophosauridae junto con Dracovenator, un grupo ubicado entre los celofísidos y los terópodos posteriores.

facts.statement: Paleontologists debated whether Dilophosaurus was a basal genus that gave rise to ceratosaurians and tetanurans, or if it was simply a large coelophysid.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos, consideraron que el Dilophosaurus podría ser un género basal que generó clados como los ceratosaurios y los tetanuros. Otros paleontólogos, piensan al contrario que en realidad este género no es más que un celofísido de gran tamaño.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus lived approximately 183 million years ago during the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages) in what is now North America.
facts.quote: vivió a principios del periodo Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 183 millones de años, entre el Sinemuriense y Pliensbachiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The genus Dilophosaurus existed from the Hettangian to the Pliensbachian stages, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Pliensbachian (201.4 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus is known from the Kayenta Formation and lived alongside dinosaurs such as Coelophysis kayentakatae and Sarahsaurus.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus es conocido de la Formación Kayenta, y vivió junto a dinosaurios como Coelophysis kayentakatae y Sarahsaurus.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was approximately 7 meters long and weighed about 400 kilograms, making it one of the first large predatory dinosaurs, though smaller than later theropods.
facts.quote: Con aproximadamente 7 m de longitud y con un peso de aproximadamente 400 kilogramos, Dilophosaurus fue uno de los primeros dinosaurios depredadores grandes, aunque más pequeño que algunos terópodos posteriores.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen weighed about 400 kg, measured about 7 meters long, and had a skull 590 mm long.
facts.quote: El espécimen más grande conocido pesaba unos 400 kg, medía unos 7 metros de largo, y su cráneo tenía 590 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was smaller, weighing approximately 283 kg, measuring 6.03 meters long, with a hip height of about 1.36 meters and a skull 523 mm long.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo es más pequeño, pesaba aproximadamente 283 kilogramos, tenía 6.03 metros de largo, con una altura de cadera de aproximadamente 1,36 metros y su cráneo tenía 523 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had a pair of longitudinal plate-like crests on its skull, similar to a cassowary with two crests.
facts.quote: Tenía un par de crestas longitudinales en forma de placa en su cráneo, similar a un casuario con dos crestas.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature of Dilophosaurus was the pair of rounded crests on its skull, possibly used for display.
facts.quote: La característica más distintiva de Dilophosaurus es el par de crestas redondeadas en su cráneo, usado posiblemente para la exhibición.

facts.statement: The teeth were long, curved, thin, and laterally compressed, with the lower jaw teeth being much smaller than those of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran largos, curvados, delgados y comprimidos hacia los lados. Los de la mandíbula inferior eran mucho más pequeños que los de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus teeth were long but had a relatively small base and expanded basally.
facts.quote: Los dientes del Dilophosaurus son largos, pero tienen una base bastante pequeña y se amplían basalmente.

facts.statement: The neck was long, with vertebrae that were hollow and very light.
facts.quote: El cuello era largo, sus vértebras eran huecas y muy ligeras.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus had 10 cervical vertebrae in the neck, 14 dorsal vertebrae in the back, and 45 caudal vertebrae in the tail.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus tenía 10 vértebras cervicales en el cuello, 14 dorsales en la espalda y 45 caudales en la cola.

facts.statement: The hands had four fingers: the first was short but strong with a large claw, the next two were longer and thinner with smaller claws, and the fourth was vestigial.
facts.quote: Las manos tenían cuatro dedos: el primero era corto pero fuerte y tenía una garra grande, los dos dedos siguientes eran más largos y delgados con garras más pequeñas, y el cuarto era vestigial.

facts.statement: Dilophosaurus was likely active and bipedal, and may have hunted large animals as well as feeding on smaller animals and fish.
facts.quote: Dilophosaurus habría sido activo y bípedo, y puede haber cazado animales grandes y también podría haberse alimentado de animales y peces más pequeños.

facts.statement: It may have grown rapidly, reaching a growth rate of 30 to 35 kilograms per year at the beginning of its life.
facts.quote: Puede haber crecido rápidamente, alcanzando una tasa de crecimiento de 30 a 35 kilogramos por año al comienzo de su vida.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen had multiple paleopathologies, including healed lesions and signs of a developmental anomaly.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo tenía múltiples paleopatologías, incluyendo lesiones cicatrizadas y signos de una anomalía del desarrollo.

facts.statement: This skull structure led to the early hypothesis that Dilophosaurus was a scavenger, with front teeth too weak to kill and hold large prey.
facts.quote: Esta conformación llevó a la hipótesis temprana que Dilophosaurus era un carroñero, con los dientes delanteros siendo demasiado débiles para derribar y sostener una presa grande.

facts.statement: Some researchers interpret trackway impressions of a Dilophosaurus-like theropod as showing feather impressions around the belly and feet, while others interpret them as sedimentary artifacts, though this does not rule out the presence of feathers.
facts.quote: Algunos investigadores han interpretado que una huella de descanso de un terópodo similar a Dilophosaurus y Liliensternus muestra impresiones de plumas alrededor del vientre y los pies, similar al plumón. Otros investigadores interpretan estas impresiones como artefactos sedimentológicos creados a medida que el dinosaurio se movía, aunque esta interpretación no descarta que el creador de huellas haya tenido plumas.
